coverage: I took the frontmatter description and every sentence of the Goal, Inventory, Booking, State control, Health metrics and Verify sections as claims, splitting compound lines (the inventory fields, the exclusive/shared booking rules, the ephemeral/shared environments line and the three Verify criteria) so that every named tool (Jira, Confluence, Enov8, Plutora, CMDB), every number (weekly refresh, nightly seed scripts) and every behaviour is checked; the skill contains no commands or flags. All three listed sources were fetched and read, and each claim was checked against all three.
suggested_edits: All three sources are overview or landing pages, not environment-management documentation: the two ISTQB pages describe the CTFL v4.0 and CTAL-TM v3.0 certifications (overview, audience, syllabus topic lists, exam structure, business outcomes) and never use the word 'environment', and tmap.net is a navigation home page whose only 'book' occurrences are its own published TMap books. None of them can confirm any claim in this skill. A fix PR should bump version and cite pages that actually document the practice: Enov8 and Plutora/Tricentis product documentation for the booking-tool claim, the ISTQB CTFL v4.0 and CTAL-TM v3.0 syllabus documents (or other pages that genuinely discuss test environments and test infrastructure) instead of the certification landing pages, and a TMap page covering test environments - or trim the skill to what the current sources support. Material and uncovered: the inventory fields, the weekly masked-copy and nightly seed-schedule figures, the exclusive vs shared booking rules, deploy consent, drift alerts, configuration as code, ephemeral per-branch environments, the four health metrics (working-hours availability, incidents, tester hours lost, mean time to restore), and the 'environment downtime is a top cause of test delay' statement.
